object_description: Pavilion-like composition of subtly offset volumes with a minimal footprint
design_condition: The building is placed peripherally at a site corner and close to the existing ice rink, using offset volumes to fit the terrain lightly while connecting the park, surrounding paths, and diverse uses.

positive.statement: The minimal building footprint is convincing and is placed credibly within the future urban context.
The subtly structured volumes create a well-proportioned lightness and a finely graduated fit into the terrain.
The pavilion-like appearance and reserved architecture establish a strong dialogue between building and landscape.
The building is well accessible from all directions through external and internal paths, while the covered entrance creates an eventful relationship with nature and the uses.
The spatial organization provides an attractively designed entrance hall with good overview and orientation.
The combination of a solid base and timber upper floor is sensible from a design perspective.
The low degree of sealing, green roof, and proposed habitats support ecological sustainability.
The location and structure of the new building provide optimal noise insulation for the open ice rink.
The project has the lowest construction costs, excellent compactness, and strong resource efficiency.

negative.statement: The proposed relocation and addition of paths and area accesses, together with the topographical interventions, require review.
Opening the edge vegetation conflicts with the character of the existing park, and the protected trees and hedges must not be loosened.
The additional tower-like cloakroom element is unnecessary and should be reconsidered.
The proposed cloakroom arrangement is neither operationally nor landscape-satisfactory and appears inaccessible and unattractive for bathers.
The parking arrangement requires further checking.
The support concept is complex, with large spans and demanding cantilevers.
The unprotected ventilated timber facade is expected to generate maintenance costs.
The proposed outdoor pool accesses, parking situation, and photovoltaic provision require further review or clarification.
